DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer` computes per-task redundancy targets, but that requirement is never enforced as a feasibility condition. `_solve_greedy()` tries to meet `target`, yet `_check_feasibility()` only checks overload, non-empty coverage, and role admissibility. In a verified probe with two models `{PM, PAR}` and one critical task, `_redundancy_target()` returned `2`, the solver assigned only the `PAR`, and `_check_feasibility()` still returned `(True, [])`. So the layer can mark a critical task “feasible” while violating its own redundancy policy.

DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector` declares convergence on total silence. If rounds contain no findings, `kappa_set()` becomes `1.0`, `kappa_rate()` also becomes `1.0` because both numerator and baseline rate are zero, `kappa_adopt()` defaults to `1.0`, and `_veto()` is false, so `converged(2)` returns `True`. I verified this directly. That contradicts the `validate_no_findings()` docstring, which says the empty-findings case should be “not converged unless null_expected.” As written, three empty rounds are treated as successful convergence.

DESCRIPTION: Most recovery actions are labels, not behavior. `get_recovery()` can return `RETRY`, `RETRY_EXTENDED`, `RETRY_CLARIFIED`, `DEGRADE`, `DOWNGRADE_ROLE`, and `LOG_ONLY`, but only `EXCLUDE` mutates internal state inside `FailureHandler`, and `process_round()` only reacts specially to `ABORT`. There is no code path that actually retries, reallocates, degrades a model, or downgrades a role. A verified probe showed repeated `UNDERPERFORM` on a PM eventually returns `DOWNGRADE_ROLE`, but nothing changes in `role_map`, so the advertised recovery policy is largely non-operative.

DESCRIPTION: `CorrelatedFailureModel` validates stored base rates via `set_base_failure_rate()`, but its override inputs are unchecked. Passing `p_i`, `p_j`, or `failure_rates` outside `[0, 1]` can make both `pairwise_joint_failure()` and `correlated_class_failure()` return impossible negative probabilities. I verified that supplying `-0.1` yields `-0.1` from both APIs, even though the docstrings promise probabilities in `[0, 1]`.

DESCRIPTION: Several public config knobs are dead API surface. `blind_first`, `theta_col`, `delta_deg`, and `default_vulnerability` are defined on `DynamicManagementConfig`, but they are never consumed anywhere else in the module. I verified one concrete case: `DynamicManagementConfig(blind_first=False)` still initializes the FSM in `BLIND`. So callers can set these fields and get no effect, with no warning that the parameter is ignored.

DESCRIPTION: `ROUND_COMPLETE` is emitted twice for the same round, and the first emission happens before the round has actually been processed. `process_round()` emits `ROUND_COMPLETE` immediately on entry, then `update_fingerprints()` emits another `ROUND_COMPLETE` after post-processing. A verified probe produced `['ROUND_COMPLETE', 'CONVERGENCE_CHECK', 'STOP_CHECK', 'ROUND_COMPLETE']`. That makes the event stream unreliable as a phase boundary for external orchestration.
